_comment: Phase ladders, keyed by id. A pack manifest references one by name via its
`phase_ladder` field; the boardroom engine resolves it at construction time.
Ladders belong to the KIND of decision, not to the domain - which is why they
live in their own registry rather than inline in pack.json. A healthcare
session deciding a pricing question should be able to borrow the pricing
`focus_warning` replaces the hardcoded product-build nudge that used to sit in
the dialogue rules. It is the one sentence that keeps a debate from skipping
ahead, and it is wrong if it talks about dev timelines in a clinical session.

product_build.label: Product build

phases.title: Product Scope & Core Feature Breakdown
phases.guidance: Define WHAT we are building, key modules, and user requirements before diving into tech stack.

phases.title: Technical Architecture, Data Pipeline & Compliance
phases.guidance: Discuss tech stack, database schemas, security, and regulatory constraints.

phases.title: Operational Execution, Cost & Go-To-Market Strategy
phases.guidance: Discuss dev timeline, team allocation, budget limits, and launch plan.

product_build.focus_warning: Do NOT jump ahead into dev timelines or infrastructure choices before defining what is actually being built.

clinical_program.label: Healthcare program

phases.title: Clinical Validity & Data Feasibility
phases.guidance: Is the clinical premise sound? What data exists, where does it live, and what is its real quality? Who is the patient population and how are they attributed?

phases.title: Compliance, Privacy & Integration
phases.guidance: Regulatory classification, PHI handling, BAAs, de-identification strategy, EHR integration path and timeline, security review posture.

phases.title: Reimbursement, Contracting & Deployment
phases.guidance: Who pays and under what mechanism, contracting path, ROI proof, pilot design, clinician adoption and workflow rollout.

clinical_program.focus_warning: Do NOT jump ahead to reimbursement or rollout before the clinical premise and the data behind it have been established.

drug_development.label: Drug development

phases.title: Target, Evidence & Development Strategy
phases.guidance: Is the target validated? What is the primary endpoint, the population, and the effect size the trial is powered to detect?

phases.title: Regulatory Path, Trial Execution & Safety
phases.guidance: Filing pathway and agency expectations, enrollment feasibility, statistical analysis plan, manufacturing readiness, and the safety commitments that follow approval.

phases.title: Access, Launch & Lifecycle
phases.guidance: Payer value story and net price, launch readiness across supply and field force, exclusivity runway and loss-of-exclusivity planning.

drug_development.focus_warning: Do NOT jump ahead to launch or forecast before the endpoint, the regulatory path, and the safety profile are settled.

research_program.label: Research program

phases.title: Target Validation & Experimental Design
phases.guidance: What is the evidence the target is real? Is the model relevant to human disease, and has the key result been reproduced independently?

phases.title: Translatability, Data Quality & Compliance
phases.guidance: Biomarkers and target engagement, batch effects and analytical rigour, sample provenance and consent, and what the lab can actually run.

phases.title: Candidate Selection, IP & Handoff
phases.guidance: Criteria for advancing a candidate, freedom to operate and filing timing, and what development needs from research to take it forward.

research_program.focus_warning: Do NOT jump ahead to candidate selection before target validation and reproducibility have been addressed.
